noInherit.description: If true, the annotation is not inherited by mixins.

condition.description:
If provided this condition expression will be evaluated for a given instance and if result is not `true` then
instance will be deemed invalid.

`@constraint(condition)` annotation can be applied to a type, a field, a parameter, or a value type. If it is specified
on a field then expression has to contain reference to this field or to `$` which is equivalent.
- when the constraint is applied to a type, the expression scope is the instance of the type
- when applied to a field, the expression scope is the instance of the type and specific value of the field is bound
   to $ variable
- when applied to a parameter, the expression scope is action arguments and specific value of the parameter is bound
   to $ variable
- when applied to a value type, $ is a value and scope is depending if parent is a field or a method

example usage:
- foo: map<@constraint(condition='"A" <= $ && $ <= "Z"]') string, @constraint(condition='$ > 42') int>
- bar: positive: constraint(condition='$ > 0') int
- baz: function(increment: @constraint(condition='$ > 0') int): int

#message could be used to provide custom error message.

message.description: Custom error message template for #condition constraint violation. See {@link Template} for more information

length.description: If defined, this string field is limited to the specified length.

required.description:
The field or function parameter must have a value to be valid, specified using the exclamation point syntax:
```type
  where: !Location
```

title:
Annotation used to specify constraints on a field or function.

Some of these are explicitly specified using the constraint annotation and some are implicitly created from DSL
syntax.  For example, the exclamation point in a field declaration maps to `@constraint(required=true)`.
name: Ann.Constraint
